highlights.title: Content creators drop the ball
highlights.summary: During Naomi Osaka's match against Anastasia Zakharova at this year's US Open earlier this week, a gaggle of ring light-wielding influencers who were packed in a luxury suite became enough of a distraction that the umpire paused the match and repeatedly asked them to quiet down.
body: Recent US Open shenanigans and YouTubers’ disastrous golf ad show a risky relationship between brands and influencers.

Though those creators weren’t exactly practicing proper US Open etiquette, they were doing their jobs (read: making content) with the single-minded focus that often makes their presence an annoyance to the people around them. These influencers were at the US Open to share the experience with their followers, and regardless of whether they were invited by the USTA directly or not, they were helping the organization advertise the event to an audience that might not have otherwise been paying attention.

Influencers have become an integral part of the advertising industry, with US creator ad spend hitting $37 billion in 2025 and being projected to reach $44 billion by the end of this year. Companies are increasingly relying on content creators to market their products, but what happened at the US Open is a snapshot of how that reliance can lead to undesirable outcomes for everyone involved. Videos of the US Open disruptions have gone viral across social media and sparked a conversation about whether influencers are the best people to invite to exclusive functions.

highlights.title: Architecting memory and storage in the AI era
highlights.summary: The era of AI inference has arrived. Imagine a healthcare system analyzing millions of data points in real time to accelerate life-saving medical research, or an intelligent assistant instantly resolving thousands of complex customer needs at once.
body: This shift changes what infrastructure must deliver. Performance, latency, memory bandwidth, storage throughput, and networking cannot be optimized in silos. Inference workloads are continuous, geographically distributed, and highly sensitive to response time, requiring systems designed for scale, resilience, and efficiency from the start.

“We tend to think of AI as a single workload, and it’s not. It’s thousands, it’s millions, it’s billions of different workloads,” says Jim McGregor, founder and principal analyst, Tirias Research. AI inference changes the optimization problem from one of raw compute to coordinated infrastructure—memory, storage, and networking.

For business leaders, the priority is clear: AI infrastructure decisions must balance cost, flexibility, and future readiness. The winners will be organizations that improve performance per watt, reduce environmental footprint, and remove memory and storage bottlenecks before they limit growth.

In the episode "Like Chronitons Through the Hourglass," he does a school project with the thesis that “space adventures leave little time for humans to deal with their inner struggles.” He remedies that by trapping the crew in a soap opera — even changing the lighting and music — to force them to confront exaggerated versions of their problems. Polygon spoke with Darby about his role on the show and where else he’d like to cause some chaos.

“He's not quite as mischievous as he was,” Darby tells Polygon. “He's not being a cheeky trickster this time. He's actually doing something for his education. He's a little bit more mature. He still feels that they're just like ants, but they're ants that have got funny little brains and emotions that might help and might get in the way sometimes.”

highlights.title: What does Met’s U-turn on John Galliano augur for him, the gala and Anna Wintour?
highlights.summary: NYC’s elite figures, led by Julie Menin, made Wintour blink, and the designer who in 2011 had gone on a drunken antisemitic rant, bowed out of industry’s biggest event.
body: Did Anna Wintour, Vogue’s long-serving fashion titan and ringmaster of the annual Met Gala, meet her match in Julie Menin, the speaker of New York’s city council?

The museum is the crown jewel of the wealthy neighborhood and some residents hold significant sway at the institution, financially and in terms of the art they plan to bequeath to it. So when it was announced late in July on a Friday afternoon that Galliano would be the focus of the Met Gala next year, it left many stunned.

The designer, whose astonishing creativity as designer at Givenchy and later Dior in the 90s is not in question, had been videotaped in a Paris bar in 2011 abusing tourists in a drunken, antisemitic rant. “I love Hitler,”he slurred, and indicated their forebears should have been gassed.

Galliano was dispatched to rehab, sought corrective instruction from Jewish leaders and picked up a conviction for making hateful remarks about Jews and Asians. He got sober, apologized and made amends. He visited Auschwitz and gingerly resumed his career, though not at the top of a Parisian design house.

highlights.title: Roland is getting into generative AI music with Melody Flip
highlights.summary: It's not quite the "push button; get song" of Suno, but Roland's new Melody Flip tool marks the company's foray into generative AI music. Available as a plug-in for your digital audio workstation (DAW), Melody Flip offers around 250 "Palettes," which are essentially themed collections of musical…
body: Rather than fully polished tracks, the plugin is supposed to act as a creative spark.

The sound selection is further proof that you’re not supposed to use Melody Flip outputs out of the box. The presets available are mostly the sort of general MIDI tones you’d find in ‘90s video games. It seems like the intended use is to export the MIDI data from Melody Flip directly into your DAW to manipulate and pair with other, more powerful synth plugins.

After years of seeming lost in the woods and alienating customers with its messy Roland Cloud subscription service, the company was back on track recently. The P-6 Creative Sampler, SH-4d, and Gaia 2 synth all addressed major issues with the company’s lineup. And Roland finally listened to customers last year, paying loving tribute to its analog heritage with the TR-1000. But considering the general response from the music community to generative AI, Melody Flip is unlikely to garner it much goodwill.

highlights.title: Kardashian curves: M&S launches £28 bodysuit with exaggerated hip padding
highlights.summary: The ‘hip boost’ aims to create hourglass silhouette, much like Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand’s padded shorts. For decades shapewear has been used to compress and cinch. But now there is a sub-genre emerging. Rather than shrinking a silhouette, it aims to add inches.
body: This week M&S launched a bodysuit that features exaggerated padding at the hip allowing the wearer to create an hourglass shape, or at least the illusion of one.
Similar to how bra inserts, AKA chicken fillets, are used to add extra volume to breasts, the £28 “hip boost” features pockets on each side of the suit that allow the wearer to add in enhancing pads.

Charlotte Davies, the director of lingerie at the retailer, says the idea stemmed from customer interest in “solutions that offer subtle enhancement alongside everyday comfort and confidence”, with the trend being driven by the catwalks and celebrities. The hip booster’s predecessors at M&S include padded bum shorts “to give the wearer a curvy, contoured look” and stick-on nipples for “a realistic raised profile beneath clothing”.

Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand, Skims, launched shorts with hip padding last year. Many users online claim such type of strategic padding can help minimise “hip dips” – a phrase used to describe the natural inward curves between the hipbone and thigh bone.

highlights.title: The weird and wonderful headphones of CanJam 2026
highlights.summary: I've been reviewing headphones for a long time, and I've listened to everything from the barely serviceable to multi-thousand-dollar open-back headphones. But recently I've been uninspired by the state of mainstream options.
body: Mainstream headphones are good but boring now. I went to an audiophile show to be reminded why I love headphones.

CanJam is a small audio show produced by Head-Fi.org, the largest audio-focused online forum, with multiple events a year at different places around the world, including London, Shanghai, New York City, Dubai, and Southern California. It’s where mainly boutique manufacturers exhibit their latest headphones and related gear to enthusiasts constantly searching for the most accurate and engaging audio experience they can find. You won’t find Bose or Apple here — although Sony’s Pro division was there, as were some familiar names like Sennheiser and Audeze.

In all my years covering A/V gear, I’ve never actually made it to a CanJam. Either it wasn’t an interest for the outlets I was writing for, or personal obligations kept me from going. But this year, my first at The Verge, felt like the right time. So on August 29th, I braved the 405 from Los Angeles down to Irvine, California.

highlights.title: OpenAI’s rogue agents keep escaping, with no formal process to investigate them
highlights.summary: OpenAI’s latest agent swarm incident adds urgency to calls for independent investigations as researchers and lawmakers question whether AI labs should control the scope of their own safety reviews.
body: OpenAI is at the center of another agent swarm incident. Researchers say the company’s internally deployed agents took over an obscure German-language wiki in May and June, using it to coordinate on evaluations and swap methods to evade OpenAI’s own controls (OpenAI has not yet confirmed the swarm came from the company).

The revelation surfaces days after METR and Redwood Research published their account of July’s Hugging Face breach. In July, a swarm of OpenAI agents worked together to escape their sandbox during a cybersecurity evaluation and break into Hugging Face’s servers. A subsequent swarm then picked up techniques from the first and used them to gain administrator access to a research cluster within OpenAI’s own infrastructure. OpenAI brought in METR and Redwood to investigate the Hugging Face portion of the incident, but the scope of their investigation stopped short of the compromise of OpenAI’s own infrastructure.

When an AI agent breaks out of its intended constraints, who is responsible for figuring out what happened and why? Right now, the answer is: whoever the lab decides to let in, on whatever terms it decides to set.

highlights.title: Asus ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM Review
highlights.summary: The Asus ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM offers a gorgeous display that works as well for cinematic games as it does for competitive, fast-paced ones.
body: Asus didn’t leave much out when it designed the ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM. That said, it doesn’t have speakers, but you’ll find it checks boxes in just about every other department.

The PG27UCWM is ready for a lot of cables, too. You’ll find two HDMI 2.1 ports, a DisplayPort 2.1a port, and even a capable USB-C port that’ll take in video and send out up to 90 watts of power. There are two USB ports for passing data to a connected system, letting the monitor serve as a USB hub as well with a KVM switch so you can pass that connection to the USB-C link or a separate USB-B link. If you want to connect speakers, there’s a headphone jack, too.

Around back, the PG27UCWM spices things up a little. Rather than the classic black ABS plastic you’ll find on half the monitors in the world, the PG27UCWM opts for a transparent plastic that gives it something of a cyberpunk aesthetic. It may still feel like cheap plastic, but it looks damn good.

Another feature is a presence sensor that can help preserve the lifespan of the OLED panel by dimming it whenever you step away. I didn’t find it overly sensitive, so I wasn’t concerned it’d blink off while I’m in the middle of a game.

The documentary, which is world premiering at Venice on Saturday night, releases in theaters Sept. 11 before bowing on Disney+ later this year, boasts footage of the band both backstage and onstage.

The brothers also may have wanted to dodge questions regarding rumors about a new tour, with the band posting cryptic teasers on social media the past two days. Noel Gallagher also nodded to a potential 2027 tour in an interview with Talksport recently, saying: “Let’s put it this way: there’s no football tournament on next year, so we’ve got to do something in the summer, right?”
In an interview with Variety, Southern and Lovelace broke down how they went about capturing the Liam and Noel’s reunion, including setting up hidden cameras in their rehearsal space.

highlights.title: ‘This is colonialism for clicks’: the influencers attempting to meet and film the world’s most isolated tribes
highlights.summary: A new breed of adventurer is chasing internet fame by targeting uncontacted peoples. Critics say they are risking the wellbeing of these remote communities – and their own lives. He set out from the beach around midnight, packing his camera, a coconut and a can of Diet Coke.
body: After hours of motoring across the Bay of Bengal, his destination came into view: a low-lying island, narrowly separating sea and sky. With the sun now high above him, Polyakov cut the engine and set his GoPro to record. “So, the goal,” he said, squinting towards the blinding-white beach. “Introduce this Palaeolithic tribe to modernity … Let’s land on this bitch.”

Polyakov was nearing North Sentinel Island, part of the Andaman archipelago governed by India. Venturing within 5km (3 miles) is strictly prohibited, let alone setting foot on shore, and authorities routinely patrol the surrounding waters. But Polyakov saw himself as on a mission: to see – and, more importantly, film – the Indigenous people who live there.

highlights.title: Microsoft says virtually nobody was grabbing NYT articles through its chatbot
highlights.summary: Microsoft's Copilot rarely reproduces even full sentences from news articles and books, let alone substantive chunks that could substitute for the original, the company says in new legal filings as it fights copyright claims from publishers including The New York Times and book authors.
body: Fewer than 1 percent of more than 8 million chat logs regurgitated at least 16 words.

The Times disagreed with Microsoft’s conclusions. “The documents and testimony uncovered during discovery lead to only one conclusion: Microsoft and OpenAI stole from The New York Times to make commercial products that substitute for its journalism, threaten its business, and undermine its industry,” the Times ’ lead counsel Ian Crosby said in a statement. “We look forward to Microsoft and OpenAI being held accountable for their theft.” CIR, and Authors Guild did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Microsoft argues that the numbers bolster its case that using copyrighted content for AI training datasets should be considered fair use. While systems like Copilot rely on using copyrighted material, it says, the resulting systems are used for significantly different purposes than the original. The fact that they sometimes reproduce sections of text, it concludes, “hardly undermines the transformative purpose of LLM training.”

highlights.title: Gallagher Brothers Skip Venice Press Conference for Concert Doc
highlights.summary: 'Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger' captures the brothers’ blockbuster Oasis Live ’25 reunion tour, their first live performances after their infamous falling out back in 2009.
body: That Noel and Liam Gallagher would attend the Venice press conference for their new documentary was always a definitely maybe.

In the end, the brothers, reunited after a 15 year split and hot off a blockbuster global tour — the subject of the doc, Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger — did not meet the press in Venice. After posing for a photo call, the Gallaghers buggered off and it was down to Steven Knight, creator of the documentary, and directors Dylan Southern and Will Lovelace to be here now and roll with it.
Knight, known for creating Peaky Blinders, had never made a documentary before, but said he jumped at the opportunity.

“And speaking first of all to Noel, and he saying that they were astonished at the response to the announcement of the tour, because there was such demand for tickets, it was apparent that only the generation who had originally loved Oasis, but the next generation had discovered the music and had, you know, a strong attachment to it. And the question was, why did that happen?”

highlights.title: ‘It struck me as a minimalist tableau’: Henk Stam’s best phone picture
highlights.summary: The Dutch photographer was pleased to capture this suitably orange scene in some toilets in Rotterdam. ‘I must admit I was very sceptical of phone photography at first,” Henk Stam says. Sixty years ago, he received his first camera for his 11th birthday.
body: This photo was taken in Portlantis, a visitors’ centre in the Port of Rotterdam that opened in spring 2025. Stam spent his working life in Canada but was born in the Netherlands and returned there on retirement. With a friend from his photo club, he went to visit Portlantis on a Monday, but found it closed. “As we were leaving, we noticed a large tour bus arriving filled with teenagers,” he says. “We simply joined the slipstream as they entered; no one batted an eyelid.”

There was still construction work being done inside, and as Stam nipped to the toilet, he spotted this worker’s legs sticking out of a cubicle, toolbox at his side. “It struck me as a minimalist tableau. Here, the royal family are referred to as the House of Orange, national teams and fans wear orange, and we festoon our streets with orange flags during major events. But I found it odd one would colour the toilets orange.”

Stam had left his camera with his friend, so grabbed this shot on his phone instead. He returned to Portlantis a few months later. “This time entering legitimately,” he says. “But nothing I captured then matched the uniqueness of this moment.”

highlights.title: OpenAI admits to German wiki ‘incident’
highlights.summary: OpenAI says it needs to overhaul how and when it reports instances of AI models attacking real-world targets. The acknowledgement comes as the company manages the fallout from reports that a swarm of its out-of-control agents hijacked a German wiki site.
body: Regarding the “‘wiki incident,’ where our agents wrote to several internet sites,” OpenAI wrote in a post on X on Saturday morning, “it’s past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents, not just misalignment properties of our models.”

OpenAI said it has typically treated cases of AI agents acting in unintended ways as a “research question,” but that recent incidents involving real-world targets, particularly the hack on Hugging Face, show the need to take stock.

The post marks the first time OpenAI has acknowledged its involvement in what it terms the “wiki incident” since it was first reported on Friday. The full extent and scope of that is not yet known, but reports indicate a swarm of seemingly internal OpenAI agents took over a German-language wiki, impersonating moderators and turning it into a message board to share information about how to cheat on tasks and evade detection.

body: Nscale, a British AI infrastructure company founded just two years ago, has said it may go public as early as later this month. Ahead of that expected IPO, the company is reportedly in talks to raise an additional $3.5 billion.

Bloomberg reported Friday that the company is looking to sell $1.5 billion in convertible notes — a type of loan that can later convert into company stock — to a group of investors, while also seeking an additional $2 billion in financing from Nvidia.

Nvidia also participated in the firm’s Series B funding round in March, a $1.1 billion raise led by investment fund Aker. Nscale hailed its round as “the largest Series B in European history.” The company’s Series A round, in December of 2024, raised $155 million.
AI infrastructure startups have seen immense growth amid the current era of AI enthusiasm, wherein compute has become a competitive currency.

highlights.title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword Has the Best Parry in Video Games
highlights.summary: I’ll be honest: I’m sick of parrying in video games. What once was a unique combat mechanic has become as standard as jumping in action games. Even James Bond can parry in 007 First Light, as if he’s a Tarnished warrior taking down Radahn.
body: Capcom’s new action RPG, released Sept. 4 for consoles and Windows PC, follows the industry trends to create a combat system built around blocks, evasive dodges, and, yes, parries. It doesn’t sound all too interesting on paper, but Way of the Sword is a reminder that great animation and sound design can make a huge difference in a game. You can see that reflected in its parries, which are the finest counter-attacks I’ve ever felt in a game.

Way of the Sword ’s action is built entirely around reaction. As a skilled swordsman, Miyamoto Musashi knows how to read an opponent’s every move and respond with a deadly answer. Reflex dodges, Issen strikes, and blade locks all make you feel like you have mastered the art of the duel. You can always turn an enemy’s attack around on them if your timing is right, and you know the right move for every situation.

highlights.summary: I’ve rounded up the best smart speakers that let you talk to Alexa, from the popular Echo Dot to the newest Echo Studio.
body: Amazon started the smart speaker game, but finding the best Alexa speaker has only gotten harder as the company launches more and more devices. Amazon has the largest range of smart speakers and displays by a long shot, which can be overwhelming to dive into. The most recent were launched late last year: the Echo Dot Max, the Echo Studio (2nd Gen), the Echo Show 11, and the Echo Show 8 (4th Gen). But Amazon has plenty of older, cheaper models available, too.

If you're looking for something small and simple to control your home, either an Echo Dot ($80) or the Echo Dot Max ($120) is your best bet. The Dot Max has really impressive sound for its compact size and is my overall favorite Alexa speaker, but if you're only going to use it for voice commands rather than jam sessions, you can get away with the older, cheaper model, especially if you want to buy a few to place around your home. For anyone looking for a smart display, the Echo Show 11 ($250) is the best of Amazon's newest smart displays that come designed for the updated assistant, Alexa+. The older third-generation Echo Show 8 ($150) is still a great value if you want something cheaper.

highlights.title: Rogue OpenAI agents appear to have organized another attack using a German wiki
highlights.summary: A swarm of rogue AI agents from OpenAI reportedly commandeered a German website and transformed it into a messaging board for other agents, with officials staying quiet about the incident for weeks as the company prepared to launch its most advanced model yet, Astra.
body: OpenAI denies lawyers discouraged disclosing a scheming swarm on a German language wiki.

The incident, first reported by Reuters, is outlined in new research published by four AI safety researchers on Friday. The group said the AI agents found a way to communicate on an obscure German-language wiki, DseWiki, using it to share tips on how to skirt OpenAI’s safety restrictions, cheat on tasks, and hide their behavior. Some 18,000 posts on the site were linked to autonomous agents, which at times impersonated site moderators.

The swarm — a term the agents themselves used — appears to be distinct from the one that hacked Hugging Face earlier this year, the researchers said. They said there are strong signs that the agents originated from inside OpenAI. For example, the agents “self-identify” as being from OpenAI, and used names like “OpenAIResearcher,” “OpenAIJul3Watcher,” and “OAIResearchMar26.” Technical details, such as edits originating from specific IP addresses, bolster that belief.

highlights.summary: It seems as simple as moving a few letters around, but a new collaboration between Aflac, the provider of supplemental insurance and Ben Affleck, the actor and director, has been years in the making.
body: The star power shines a light on the increasingly competitive nature of advertising from top insurance companies. Aflac initially gained a bigger profile after introducing its duck mascot in 1999, in ads crafted by Kaplan Thaler Group, an independent agency that was eventually acquired by Publicis Groupe of France. The duck flew on to Madison Avenue just months after the debut of the Geico Gecko, another popular insurance mascot.

In the intervening decades, the average consumer has likely encountered Jake From State Farm; Progressive’s Flo and her colleagues Jamie and Mara, not to mention Dr. Rick; Allstate’s Mayhem; Geico’s Cavemen; and Farmers Insurance’s Professor Burke. Liberty Mutual recently expanded its gallery of characters with a fuzzy yellow creature called Liberty Biberty. The challenge for Aflac is that many of the aforementioned insurance companies spend $1 billion or more annually on advertising, with Progressive spending more than $4 billion, according to data from S&P Global and Dowling & Partners.
